topics.title: Equilibrium, excess demand and excess supply

concepts.learning_objective: Define market equilibrium, equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity in a perfectly competitive market.
Identify excess demand and excess supply at a price and describe equilibrium as zero excess demand and zero excess supply.
Explain how the 'Invisible Hand' moves price towards equilibrium when the market is out of equilibrium.

topics.title: Equilibrium with a fixed number of firms

concepts.learning_objective: Show that with a fixed number of firms, equilibrium lies at the intersection of the market demand and market supply curves.
Calculate equilibrium price, equilibrium quantity and excess demand or supply from linear demand and supply equations.

topics.title: Wage determination in the labour market

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a profit-maximising firm hires labour until the wage equals the marginal revenue product of labour and why labour demand slopes downward.
Explain the backward-bending individual labour supply curve and the upward-sloping market supply of labour.
Describe how the wage rate is determined where labour demand by firms equals labour supply by households.
Analyse how a shift in the demand curve changes equilibrium price and quantity with a fixed number of firms.
Analyse how a shift in the supply curve changes equilibrium price and quantity with a fixed number of firms.
Predict which effects of simultaneous shifts in demand and supply are certain and which depend on the size of the shifts.

topics.title: Market equilibrium with free entry and exit

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why free entry and exit make the equilibrium price equal to the minimum average cost of firms.
Calculate the equilibrium quantity and the equilibrium number of firms under free entry and exit.
Compare the effect of a demand shift under free entry and exit with that under a fixed number of firms.

topics.title: Applications: price ceiling and price floor

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the effects of a price ceiling below the equilibrium price, including shortage, rationing and black markets.
Explain the effects of a price floor above the equilibrium price, including excess supply and government purchase of the surplus.
